checked_sources: Shimada, Lattices of Algebraic Cycles on Fermat Varieties in Positive Characteristics (2001), DOI:10.1112/S0024611500012673
correctness.rationale:
If p^nu≡−1 modN and N≥3 then -1 has order 2 in cyclic

; hence d=ord_N(p) is even and its unique order-2 element is p^(d/2), so nu≡d/2 mod d. Harashita Lemma 7.7 provides the diagonal Fermat quotient with cover degree e^(2m+1), e=(q+1)/N prime to p, and Proposition 7.9 gives the exact p-local q^m bound and ℓ-adic unimodularity for ℓ∤e. Plugging in minimal q=p^(d/2) proves the reported bound. Fresh independent modular examples (2,3),(2,5),(3,7),(2,17) reproduced the order-half relation. The bound is not asserted sharp for the lattice itself.
residual_risks: The p-local bound need not equal actual saturation exponent; no claim of exact exponent or optimality among arbitrary cycle generators.
Other choices of cycles may improve the bound even though selected q minimizes this published construction.
Source directly proves uniform q^m result; label/parameter optimization does not avoid prior coverage.

originality.rationale: FAIL: Harashita Corollary 7.8 and Proposition 7.9 already establish the Fermat quotient and p-adic saturation statements for every q=p^nu with N | q+1. The order-half identity is elementary cyclic-group arithmetic, and optimizing this explicit monotone power q^m over admissible q is forced. Thus every scientific claim is an immediate instance of the stronger published parameter-uniform source result, despite source not writing multiplicative-order notation.
